 Print IndiGo passenger's photo before being deboarded after emergency braking in Bengaluru Screenshot Bengaluru: A Madurai-bound IndiGo flight carrying passengers from Bengaluru had a close shave on Monday morning after the pilot aborted take-off moments before the aircraft was to become airborne, following an alleged hydraulic system failure. Flight 6E 6526, scheduled to depart Kempegowda International Airport (KIA) at 7.20am, was accelerating on the runway after receiving clearance for take-off when the crew detected a technical snag. The pilot immediately applied the brakes. As the aircraft came to a screeching stop, cabin crew members announced, “Heads down… heads down,” triggering moments of anxiety among passengers. While some instinctively ducked for cover, others were left wondering what had gone wrong. The crew subsequently informed passengers that the aircraft had developed a technical snag and the captain had decided against proceeding with the take-off. The aircraft remained on the runway for nearly 30 minutes before passengers were deboarded and taken to the terminal building. They were subsequently accommodated and the flight took off for Madurai at 9:20 am. Passenger M Balasubramaniam, a businessman residing at Dollars Colony in Bengaluru and a former pilot, told The Times of India that the pilot’s timely intervention had potentially averted a potential disaster. “Moments before the take-off, the aircraft was stopped by emergency braking. The pilot’s quick thinking and decision has to be appreciated. I think he averted a big disaster; he did a fantastic job. We were told that the hydraulic system failure indicator was on and the captain acted in the nick of time,” he said. Join conversation

 Describing the incident as serious, Balasubramaniam said the crew handled the situation professionally and there was no panic onboard. “Even during deplaning, Capt Gautam and team apologised to the passengers for the inconvenience,” he added. A frequent flyer, Balasubramaniam raised concerns over aircraft maintenance and operational safety. Pointing to successful emergency braking, another passenger said: “we hope a probe is undertaken by both IndiGo management and DGCA into the incident.”
